book_meta.subtitle_child: My First Bengali IPA Sound Book

ipa_key.name: Tied Affricate
ipa_key.kid_desc: Start with your tongue stopping the air, then slide straight into a 'shh' train sound!
ipa_key.parent_desc: The tie-bar above /t͡ʃ/ links /t/ (stop closure) and /ʃ/ (postalveolar release) into one single consonant sound.

ipa_key.name: Aspiration (Mahaprana)
ipa_key.kid_desc: Blow a strong gust of wind out of your mouth right as the sound pops!
ipa_key.parent_desc: Superscript [ʰ] marks a strong voiceless burst of air immediately following the release of the consonant.

ipa_key.name: Dental Stop
ipa_key.kid_desc: Press the flat tip of your tongue gently against the back of your top front teeth.
ipa_key.parent_desc: The bridge diacritic beneath /t̪/ means the tongue tip touches the upper teeth, unlike English alveolar /t/.

ipa_key.name: Open Central Vowel
ipa_key.kid_desc: Open your mouth wide like a yawn and say a bright 'aaah'!
ipa_key.parent_desc: An open central-to-front unrounded vowel, similar to 'a' in 'father' but slightly brighter.

sound_recipe.label: 1. Tongue Roof Seal
sound_recipe.detail: Press tongue blade behind the top gum ridge to block the air.

sound_recipe.label: 2. Tied Hushing Release
sound_recipe.detail: Release the seal directly into a crisp 'sh' channel (linked by the top tie-bar).

sound_recipe.label: 3. Big Wind Burst
sound_recipe.detail: Push a strong puff of breath out with the release!

articulation.voicing: Voiceless (vocal cords stay open and silent)

word_breakdown.note: Full affricate closure released with a strong puff of air.
Vertical vowel sign following ছ that shifts the inherent vowel to open /a/.
Tongue tip touches the back of the upper front teeth (marked by the under-bridge in /t̪/) with zero aspiration.
Ends the word on an open, relaxed /a/ vowel.

mouth_placement_steps: Flatten the blade of the tongue (just behind the tip) and press it firmly against the post-alveolar ridge (the bumpy roof of the mouth just behind the upper teeth).
Keep the vocal cords completely relaxed and open (no throat vibration) while building air pressure behind the tongue seal.
Pull the tongue slightly back into a narrow groove to release the built-up air as a sharp '/t͡ʃ/' ('ch' sound) fused with an immediate, audible gust of breath ('ʰ').

coaching_game.title: The Paper Umbrella Puff Test
coaching_game.setup: Hold a lightweight strip of tissue paper (our 'paper umbrella') 2 inches in front of your child's lips.
coaching_game.action: Have your child say /t͡ʃʰ/ and then the full word ছাতা (/t͡ʃʰat̪a/).
coaching_game.success_cue: On the very first sound /t͡ʃʰ/, the tissue strip should visibly leap forward from the burst of air (ʰ), then settle completely still during the second syllable /t̪a/!

common_pitfalls.fix: English speakers naturally aspirate initial 'ch' lightly, which makes it easy to under-emphasize Bengali /t͡ʃʰ/. Exaggerate the puff of air so the child feels the cool wind on the back of their hand.

common_pitfalls.issue: Sliding into a Pure Fricative [s] or [ʃ]
common_pitfalls.fix: In fast or regional speech, the initial stop closure /t/ in /t͡ʃʰ/ is sometimes skipped, turning ছাতা into [sat̪a]. Remind the learner that the tongue must first seal the roof of the mouth completely (the 't' in /t͡ʃʰ/) before releasing the air.

common_pitfalls.issue: Using an English Alveolar /t/ on the Second Syllable (/t̪a/)
common_pitfalls.fix: Watch the dental bridge in /t͡ʃʰat̪a/! After the post-alveolar /t͡ʃʰ/, the tongue tip must move forward to touch the upper front teeth for /t̪/, keeping it crisp and unaspirated.
